With this small of a community I thought it would be interesting to hear about the different programs or degrees that everyone is involved in.

Bonus points if you share any thoughts on what you'd like to see in this subverse.
What is your degree/area of study and what would you like to see in this subverse?

Well I just finished my Master's in Math and now I'm starting a PhD in Engineering Mechanics.

I'm not sure what I'd like to see exactly, however, I hope this subverse stays positive. I know a lot of people tend to complain about their experiences in graduate school but all of my experiences have been positive. I enjoy grad school much more than I did undergrad.

I just finished my first year of a Materials Science PhD program. So far, it's been pretty much non-stop fun with the exception of written quals, which were really stressful.

I think it would be great to give this subverse as much of a positive theme as possible -- not to say that we shouldn't discuss struggles with grad school, but that we should try to keep the atmosphere supportive.

I'm one semester from completing my English Master's (concentrating on rhetoric and composition), and hoping to enter into a PhD program in Humanities (focus on literary studies [and specifically Japanese]) next year.

It's mostly the fellowship of getting to speak to others about your experiences and plans (and generally talking about oneself) that I like.
Very cool - out of curiosity, why Japanese? Is it for heritage/cultural reasons, or are you planning to work there later perhaps?

Thank you! Of all national literatures I've studied, it appeals to me most--the absolutely unique literary history makes for a range of areas to study, from a female-dominant Heian period to the isolationist floating world of the Edo period to the frantic influence of the Meiji (and I still haven't decided which era I /really/ want to stick with, because I love them all).

There's also so much rich overlap with other areas I'm into--aesthetics, paleography, book history, reception history and arts/crafts movements, for example--that Japan is perfect for me in the interdisciplinary context of the degree.

I am almost done with my Master's in Social Work with a focus on mental health.

I like the idea of a supportive area to discuss grad school. Grad school is difficult and sometimes what we need as far as support is to vent. But I think I'd like to see an overall positive atmosphere to keep people coming back.
